People LARGE and CLOSE, chest up, heads at about one fifth from the top of the frame. Every person is FULLY inside the frame: heads complete with clear empty space above them, nobody cropped at the neck, shoulders or waist, nobody touching the left or right edges.
setting: Setting: a small neighborhood bakery (padaria) in Brazil in the 1960s: a brick wood-fired oven, metal bread trays, jute flour sacks, a glass display counter, a hand-crank cash register, a slate chalkboard, white cloth aprons and baker's caps.

images.scene: The owner, a man in his fifties in a white cloth apron over a rolled-sleeve shirt, standing in the open doorway of the bakery at dawn, facing the camera straight on, arms crossed over his chest, jaw set, a stern unblinking stare directly into the lens. He is the subject, large and close, whole head visible with clear empty space above it; the glass counter and the oven behind him dissolve into the light.

The wooden cash drawer of a hand-crank cash register pulled fully OPEN on the bakery counter, seen from close and slightly above, VERY LARGE, filling the lower two thirds of the frame from edge to edge: the drawer almost EMPTY, only two crumpled banknotes and a few loose coins in the compartments; behind it a stack of empty metal bread trays with crumbs. The banknotes are plain and unreadable. Hard raking side light. NO PEOPLE anywhere in the frame, no hands, no faces, no aprons: a still life of objects only.

A slate chalkboard price list hanging on the bakery wall behind the counter, seen from close and straight on, VERY LARGE, filling the frame from the left edge to the right edge and extending past the bottom edge. On the slate, a column of bread prices written in chalk: each price has been crossed out and rewritten several times with a different figure squeezed next to it, older figures half-wiped into smeared chalk ghosts, the whole board a mess of corrections; the numbers are handwritten chalk digits only, roughly legible as numbers but no words. A stub of chalk and a dusty rag in the tray at the bottom. THE UPPER PART OF THE SLATE IS OVEREXPOSED and dissolves softly into the white haze at the top: NO visible top edge, NO top frame, NO wall line; only the lower frame and the chalk tray are visible. NO PEOPLE anywhere in the frame, no hands, no faces, no aprons: a still life of objects only.

A tall jute flour sack standing upright on the bakery tile floor with a long TEAR down its side, flour pouring out of the tear in a continuous thin stream and piling into a white mound on the floor; seen from close, the sack VERY LARGE, filling the lower two thirds of the frame from edge to edge, its top just below the bright haze.
